newsitem.title: USA: GCA March coffee stock data bullish, analysts say.
newsitem.headline: GCA March coffee stock data bullish, analysts say.

text.p: New York coffee futures will probably get a boost after monthly inventory data released late Tuesday showed a smaller-than-expected increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks, traders and analysts said.
"It was surprisingly low," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "We should be up sharply tommorrow."
Supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses rose in March by 111,000 60-kg bags, to 1,657,000 bags, Green Coffee Association of New York reported.
Most analysts had forecast an increase of between 250,000 and 300,000 bags after Latin America shipped heavily over the last several weeks to take advantage of higher futures prices.
"It is much smaller than expected," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "It says coffee is being absorbed rather than allowed to build stocks. The implication is bullish."
Port of New Orleans posted the largest gain in coffee stocks. New Orleans stocks rose by 74,000 bags to 551,000 bags, the GCA said.

Inventories increased by 37,000 bags to 319,000 bags in Laredo, Texas, a major receiving point for Mexican coffee. Warehouse stocks in San Francisco also increased in March, rising 24,000 bags to 141,000 bags.
In Houston, however, inventories decreased by 36,000 bags to 158,000 bags.
Additionally, some analysts worried that many Latin American countries may have little coffee left to sell after recent aggressive shipments.
"This is it for the stock increases," said Merrill's Ganes. "After this it's all downhill, as far as stocks go."
But other analysts said that while the stock data are likely to underpin the market, coffee prices will probably have a tough time staying above the key $2 per pound level.
"It is supportive," said Allendale Commodities analyst Jim Cordier, "but I think the market will continue to run into technical selling, which is what the market ran into today."
Tuesday, spot May delivery surged to a session high of 201.50 cents a lb before finishing at 192.40 cents, down 3.60 cents on the day.

After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were unchanged, at 80,828 60-kg bags as of April 14. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said. --Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk, 1 212 859 1640
